Car Sales Oct 2026 - Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Hyundai, Kia, Toyota, MG, Skoda, Honda, Renault

KS
By Kabir Sharma Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist • via Rushlane.com Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Rushlane.com Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • After taking a look at the two wheeler sales , let us now take a look at the car sales, which have reached 5,24,226 units in October 2026, up 12.18% from 4,67,289 units in October 2025.
  • Maruti Suzuki accounted for nearly half of the 64,769 units added over September, while Tata Motors and Mahindra finished just 556 units apart in the race for second place.
  • Official reporting verified via Rushlane.com news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • KABIR SHARMA Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist

Bharat NCAP Safety Standards & Indian Road Readiness

In India's rapidly evolving automotive landscape, crashworthiness and real-world durability are driving consumer purchase decisions like never before. As reported by Rushlane.com, indigenous automakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra are setting global safety benchmarks while optimizing suspension and ground clearance for unpredictable road conditions.

Big Picture: Upcoming monthly FADA retail delivery reports and Bharat NCAP rating scorecards will reveal which domestic models capture mass-market dominance.

After taking a look at the two wheeler sales , let us now take a look at the car sales, which have reached 5,24,226 units in October 2026, up 12.18% from 4,67,289 units in October 2025. Maruti Suzuki accounted for nearly half of the 64,769 units added over September, while Tata Motors and Mahindra finished just 556 units apart in the race for second place.

📌 The Core Development

Maruti Suzuki led with 2,12,384 units, up 20.46% YoY and 16.80% MoM. Its volumes increased by 36,066 units over October last year and by 30,546 units over September. With sales growing faster than the overall market in both comparisons, Maruti’s share rose to 40.51%, from 37.73% a year ago and 39.58% in September.

Tata Motors retained second place with 73,894 units, up 20.87% YoY and 7.39% MoM. Its market share increased to 14.10% from 13.08% a year earlier. However, Tata’s monthly volume growth lagged the overall market, pulling its share down from September’s 14.98%.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Mahindra sold 73,338 units, up 2.39% YoY and 14.43% MoM. It added 9,246 units over September, against Tata’s gain of 5,084 units. That narrowed Tata’s lead from 4,718 units in September to 556 in October. Mahindra’s market share edged up from 13.95% to 13.99% month on month, while remaining below the 15.33% it held in October 2025.

Hyundai placed fourth with 62,799 units, up 16.74% YoY and 9.85% MoM. Its share rose to 11.98% from 11.51% a year ago, but fell from 12.44% in September. Kia followed with 33,462 units, up 13.22% YoY and 4.51% MoM. Kia’s share stood at 6.38%, compared with 6.32% a year earlier and 6.97% in September.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Toyota recorded 29,521 units, up 17.96% MoM but down 26.67% from the 40,257 units it sold a year ago. Its share improved from 5.45% in September to 5.63% in October, against 8.62% in October 2025. Toyota posted the largest year-on-year volume decline among the manufacturers listed, selling 10,736 fewer units.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

JSW MG held seventh place with 8,013 units, up 25.26% YoY and just five units below September. Skoda followed at 7,805 units, down 5.42% YoY but up 27.91% MoM. Honda was just 196 units behind Skoda at 7,609 units. Honda’s sales grew 19.00% YoY and 70.41% MoM, lifting its market share from 0.97% in September to 1.45% in October.

Renault rounded out the top 10 with 4,577 units, down 2.03% YoY but up 34.66% MoM. Nissan sold 3,594 units, up 37.44% YoY and 8.91% MoM. Its share increased to 0.69% from 0.56% a year earlier.
